name: pydantic-subclass-fields-dropped-on-dump-komposer
behavioral_change: In Pydantic V1, dumping a model serialized every field of the runtime subclass instance held in a field annotated with a base class. In V2, only the fields declared on the annotated type are emitted, so subclass-specific fields are silently dropped from the output.
downstream_effect: The downstream project's `List` model declares `items: list[Item]` while the values are Deployment, Service, ConfigMap and Ingress subclasses, so the entire `spec` subtree of every generated Kubernetes object disappears from the rendered manifest. The five failures in tests/core/base_test.py are whole-manifest dict inequalities showing a missing `spec` key, with no exception, no library stack frame, and no mention of serialization, SerializeAsAny or subclasses.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes the field annotation in komposer/types/kubernetes.py:262 to `items: list[SerializeAsAny[Item]] = []` and imports `SerializeAsAny` from pydantic.
documented_in: The Pydantic V2 migration guide (docs/migration.md, tag v2.5.3) announces that dumping now includes only fields defined on the annotated type and links to the serialization docs (docs/concepts/serialization.md, section "Serializing with duck-typing"), which state that the old behavior can be preserved with `SerializeAsAny` and show the `as_any: SerializeAsAny[User]` annotation form in a code block.

log_mentions.reason: genuine upstream output: deprecation warnings for the V1 .json() method that the production code still calls
